Modern Periodic Law In 1912, Mosley developed a periodic law modifying Mendeleev's periodic law. It states physical and chemical properties of the elements are the periodic function of their nu mbers.
Cause of Periodicity The reoccurrence of similar properties of the elemenb after the certain regular intervals they are arranged in the order of increasing atomic numbers is called periodicity.
Description of long form of the Periodic Table Period: The horizontal row of periodic table is known as period. There are seven period. period starts with a different principal quantum number.
First period: Here, n = 1 and it contains only two elements i.e. hydrogen and helium. So called very short period.
Second period: Here, n = 2 and it contains eight elements. It starts from Li (Z=3) to (Z=IO). It is called short period.
Third period: Here; n = 3 and it also contains eight elements. It starts from Na (Z=ll) to (Z=18). It is also called short period.
Fourth period: Here, n = 4 and it contains eighteen elements from K (Z=19) to Kr (Z=36). Itg called long period.
Fifth period: Here, n = 5 and contains eighteen elements from Rubidium (Z=37) to Xenon (Z=54).It is also called long period.
Sixth period: Here, n = 6 and contains 32 elements from Cesium (Z=55) to Radon (Z=86). Iti called very long period.
Seventh period: Here, n = 7 and expected 32 elements. It is also called very long period.

Group: The vertical column of periodic table is known as a group. There are eighteen groupsc a periodic table. According to IUPAC system, these groups are numbered from 1 to 18, butr the USA system, these are named as group IA to V IIA and group VIII. Similarly, group IBt V 11B and zero (O) group.
Representative or normal elements: The elements having electrons in s and p orbital are knobl as representative elements.
Transition elements: The elemenb having electron in d-orbital are known as transition elements.
Inner-transition elements: The lanthanide and actinide series elements of periodic table known as inner-transition elements.
Lanthanide Series: Lanthanum (57) to Lutetium (71)
Actinide Series: Actinium (89) to Lawrencium (103)
